release: v1.851 VAR Layer-B Selection Decomposition & Interpretation Correction

decision_still_valid.reason: The preregistered selection rule requires the complete Layer A + Layer B procedure to pass the gate. That rule is not modified after the fact, so the v1.85 decision stands.

clarification.layer_A_explanation: Layer A estimates the VAR at the known true lag. Under the null DGP and correct specification, rejection frequency is the finite-sample size of the diagnostic.
clarification.layer_B_explanation: Layer B selects the lag by the platform BIC rule before the diagnostic. When the selected lag is below the true lag the selected VAR is underfitted and residual whiteness need not hold, so Layer B rejections are not all Type-I errors and are not a pure diagnostic test size.
clarification.joint_distribution_note: Cell-level selected-lag frequencies and overall rejection rates are observed, but their replication-level joint distribution was not retained; conditional rejection rates cannot be reconstructed from the frozen aggregate artifact.

superseded_wording.original: No candidate is sufficiently calibrated under the full selection-plus-diagnostic procedure
superseded_wording.clarified: No candidate satisfied the preregistered joint procedure gate under the full selection-plus-diagnostic procedure; Layer B rejection frequencies are procedure rejection rates, not pure diagnostic size.

interpretation_summary.edgerton_shukur_f: Conditional fixed-lag calibration strong (Layer A); the full BIC-selection procedure did not satisfy the preregistered activation gate. Not a validated replacement; not activated.
interpretation_summary.pt_adjusted: Failed the current preregistered platform-level gate and also performed poorly in fixed-lag Layer A relative to ES. This does not mean the PT statistic is invalid.
interpretation_summary.bg_lm: Failed the preregistered platform-level gate and performed poorly in fixed-lag Layer A relative to ES.
interpretation_summary.bic: No claim is made that BIC is invalid or should be replaced; lag-selection behaviour is a subject for a future preregistered program.
